sum: A low, quiet village walk east of Pokhara: three hilltop nights at Kalikasthan, Shaklung and Chisapani, never above about 1,400 m, ending on the shore of Begnas Lake.
reach: By tourist bus (7–9 hours) or by air (about 25 minutes).

guide.note: The Royal Trek runs through farmland along the southern edge of the Annapurna Conservation Area, outside it as far as we can tell, and no permit post on the route checks for a guide. A guide is worth having all the same: the route is a web of village paths and farm roads with no signs for trekkers, and the homestays need a phone call in Nepali before you turn up.

access: Both ends are close to Pokhara. The walk starts where the Prithvi Highway crosses the Bijayapur Khola, twenty to thirty minutes east of Lakeside by taxi, and ends at the bus stand below the dam at Begnas Lake, 30 to 45 minutes from the city. Kalikasthan and most of the other villages are on dirt roads, so a jeep can bring you in or out part-way.

photo.a: Begnas Lake lies below a green hillside dotted with trees and a few farmhouses, with forested hills on the far shore under large white clouds.
photo.c: Begnas Lake, where the Royal Trek ends

transportText: Tourist bus between Kathmandu and Pokhara both ways
transportExtra: the taxi to Bijayapur and the bus back from Begnas Lake
tips: Have your guide or agency phone each homestay a day ahead. Outside the busy months the family may be in the fields or away in Pokhara.
Start walking by eight. The ridges have little shade, and the mountains are sharpest before the haze builds.
Carry water and something for lunch each day; tea shops are few between the villages.

Agencies routinely add an ACAP permit and a TIMS card to this trek. As far as we can map it, the route stays in the outer wards of Pokhara and in Rupa Rural Municipality, south of the conservation area, and it has no checkpost. We found no official ruling either way, so ask what the charge is for.
Bring a sleeping bag liner, a torch and small notes. Nobody on the route can change a large one.

days.t: Drive to Bijayapur, walk to Kalikasthan
days.note: A short taxi ride east of Pokhara. The path crosses flat rice fields beside the Bijayapur Khola, then climbs about 450 m through terraces and farm villages to a ridge, which it follows eastwards to Kalikasthan. It is hot work after ten in the morning, so start early.

The longest day, mostly easy ridge walking with the mountains on your left: through forest to the hilltop of Thulakot, on past the tea shops at Mati Thana and the villages of Naudanda and Lipini, then a steep last climb through trees to Shaklung. Parts of the way now follow a dirt road.

The roughest day. A steep descent of about 600 m on steps and worn clay leads south to a saddle with a big shade tree and a few tea shops, where trails cross. From there the path climbs nearly as far again, round the back of the hill, to Chisapani. The temple on the knoll above the village looks down on the lakes.

days.t: Chisapani to Begnas Lake, drive to Pokhara
days.note: Follow the ridge west for an hour or so, then go down a long flight of stone steps to the stream that feeds Rupa Lake. Cross the rice fields and climb 200 m on a wide path to Sundari Danda, the ridge between the two lakes. Begnas Bazaar is fifteen minutes below, with buses and taxis to Pokhara.
